The five primary slash commands — **`/ship`**, **`/review`**, **`/refactor`**,

hooks, scripts, and user muscle memory all depend on these names. They will

Structured Prompt-Driven Development (persistent feature specs, INVEST-style

WITHOUT pivoting the command surface. Source: research note

## Intent → command mapping

Match what the user actually says. When the user types one of these signals, invoke the matching pipeline entry-point as your **first action**, before any other tool call or reply.

The primary user-facing surface is exactly five slash commands:

| User intent / phrasing | Invoke |
|---|---|
| Any code change: "implement", "build", "add", "fix", "ship", "release", "ready to merge", "verify", "is this done", bug reports, failing tests | `/ship` (default `auto`; pass `strict` to force explicit approvals) |
| "review this", "look at this diff/PR", severity-first review of existing code without running the full pipeline | `/review` |
| "refactor", "clean up", "restructure", "extract", "rename", "split this up", "tidy" | `/refactor` |
| "audit", "health check", "overall state of…", project-wide review with no code change | `/audit` |
| "research", "brainstorm", "investigate", "I'm stuck", "explore options before planning", library/API scoping | `/research` |

> **Zero-setup default**: the pipeline works directly from the marketplace install with no scaffolding step. Vendoring assets into a consumer repo for CI (which does not load Claude Code plugins) is a manual one-off — copy `scripts/`, `.claude/rules/`, and `docs/templates/` into the consumer repo and pin the plugin version.

> **Skills (no slash)**: per-phase logic that previously had its own slash command is now reachable only via skills. Invoke by skill name through the `Skill` tool: `reset` (clear `.claude/workflow-state/active`), `requirement-analysis` (planning specs, used by `planner`), `code-review` (used by `reviewer`), `test-gen` (used by `tester`), `static-analysis` (used by `verifier`), `research` (used by `researcher`), `release` (cut a release: SemVer bump + CHANGELOG rewrite + manifest sync + annotated tag, triggers: "cut a release", "bump tag", "tag v…", "ship a release", "release this"), `fcis-architecture`, `pragmatic-review-checklist`. The following skills are reference/process material that the pipeline agents invoke internally; users should not need to call them directly:

- `requirement-analysis` — used by `planner`
- `fcis-architecture` — used by `planner` and `reviewer`
- `code-review` — used by `reviewer`
- `pragmatic-review-checklist` — used by `reviewer` (advisory second pass on medium/high risk)
- `static-analysis` — used by `verifier`
- `test-gen` — used by `tester`
- `refactor` — used by `/refactor`
- `research` — used by `researcher`
- `release` — invoked directly by users on release-cut intents ("cut a release", "bump tag", "tag v…", "ship a release", "release this")

## Run-ID isolation contract

Every primary command (`/ship`, `/audit`, `/review`, `/research`,
`/refactor`) mints a `RUN_ID` at step 0 and exports `RUN_ID` and
`RUN_DIR` (= `docs/aidp/runs/<RUN_ID>`) into the environment of every
subagent it dispatches. All per-run artifacts — plans, specs,
research notes, review/test/verify reports, refactor
reports, gate logs, retry hints — are written under `${RUN_DIR}/`.

Run artifacts live under `docs/aidp/`; checked-in plugin docs
(`docs/templates/`, `docs/specs/`, `docs/schemas/`, `docs/reference/`,
`docs/superpowers/`) stay where they are.

This makes concurrent runs (two `/ship` sessions on the same repo, CI
+ local, two worktrees) safe by construction: each run has its own
artifact tree.

Discovery is done through three pointers, all maintained atomically
by the orchestrator's step 0:

- `docs/aidp/latest` — symlink to the active run's directory.
- `docs/aidp/latest.txt` — text fallback containing the active run-id.
- `.claude/workflow-state/active` — text file containing the active
  run-id; consumed by hooks that need to find the per-run
  workflow-state file.

Resolution order at the consumer side: `RUN_ID` env →
`.claude/workflow-state/active` → `docs/aidp/latest` → `docs/aidp/latest.txt`.
All four go through `scripts/parse-run-id.sh` before any path is
constructed (parse, don't validate). See
`docs/specs/run-id-isolation.md` for the full spec.

### Upstream phases are sequential by data dependency

The `/ship` pipeline fans out only the *read-only* verification gates
(typecheck, lint, security) inside `scripts/run-verification-gates.sh`.
The upstream phases — optional `research` → `plan` → `implement` →
`review` — remain sequential because each phase consumes the prior phase's
artifact:

- `plan` reads `${RUN_DIR}/research/<topic>.md` (when present).
- `implement` reads `${RUN_DIR}/current-plan.md`.
- `review` reads the `## Implementation` section of `${RUN_DIR}/current-plan.md` plus the diff (the standalone impl-summary.md was folded into current-plan.md on 2026-05).

Parallelizing any of these would force a phase to read an artifact
its upstream has not yet produced. Do not attempt it without first
breaking the data dependency.

## Required gates

Per `.claude/rules/release-and-verification.md`:

- A plan (produced by the `planner` agent under `/ship`) is required before implementation.
- Risk tier `medium` or `high` requires explicit human approval before implementation.
- Release gate (the `verifier` agent under `/ship`, or the `static-analysis` skill standalone) is required before declaring a change "done".

These are the thoughts that mean **STOP — you are skipping the pipeline**. Every one of them is forbidden as a reason to bypass a skill.

| Rationalization | Reality |
|---|---|
| "This is just a quick fix." | The pipeline classifies risk; you don't. Run `/ship`. |
| "I just need to read the file first." | Skills tell you HOW to read and what to look for. Invoke first. |
| "The user didn't ask for a plan." | A plan is required by repo policy regardless of phrasing — `/ship` produces one via `planner`. |
| "I'll plan in my head and skip the plan step." | Plans are artifacts. In-head plans don't pass the gate. |
| "I already know the answer." | The pipeline isn't for you; it's for the verifiable record. |
| "This is too small for the workflow." | Small things grow. The cost of running the skill is near-zero. |
| "Let me explore first, then decide." | Exploration without a skill burns context. Invoke, then explore. |
| "The test is obviously broken, I'll just fix it." | Bug → `requirement-analysis` first. No exceptions. |
| "Refactor is just moving code." | `/refactor` has its own pre/post gates for a reason. |
| "It's only adding one line." | Then the plan will be one paragraph. Run `/ship`. |

## How to invoke

- **User typed a slash command** (`/ship`, `/review`, `/refactor`, `/audit`, `/research`): the harness already dispatches it. Do not narrate or attempt to re-invoke via the `Skill` tool — just let it run.
- **User expressed an intent without a slash command**: invoke the matching skill via the `Skill` tool (e.g. `code-review`, `requirement-analysis`, `reset`). For the five primary slash commands, the skill listing exposes them under the same name (`audit`, `refactor`, `research`, …) — invoke that skill name directly.

Never use `Read` to load `SKILL.md` files manually.

## Non-coding requests

If the user's message is clearly non-coding ("what's the weather", "what's 2+2"), no pipeline skill applies. Respond directly. The 1%-match rule is about *coding intent*, not paranoia.

## Priority

1. User's explicit instructions in CLAUDE.md or the current message — highest priority.
2. This meta-skill and the pipeline rules in `.claude/rules/` — override default model behavior.
3. Default Claude Code behavior — lowest priority.

# Plan: `/audit standards` — Pattern Discovery Subcommand

## Context

The ai-dev-pipeline plugin currently has two kinds of conventions in play:
**declared rules** (`.claude/rules/*.md` — FC/IS, parse-don't-validate,
security-baseline, etc., shipped with the plugin) and **the implicit
conventions a real codebase grows over time** (how this repo writes HTTP
handlers, what error-handling shape its tests use, which import style
dominates). The planner and reviewer have no way to see the second category —
they can only act on what the plugin's rules tell them. Every new plan
re-derives the consumer's own conventions from scratch, producing
inconsistent suggestions and longer plan output because the conventions are
restated rather than referenced.

This plan adds a `/audit standards` subcommand that scans the consumer repo,
detects recurring structural patterns per code role (HTTP handlers, jobs,
tests, etc.), and surfaces each high-confidence pattern through
`AskUserQuestion` so the user can promote it into the consumer's own
`.claude/rules/<name>.md`. Once promoted, the rule is `@`-imported by the
consumer's `CLAUDE.md` and becomes available to every planner invocation; the
planner can then write "follows `<name>.md`" instead of re-deriving the
convention. The expected token-saving effect lives on the **output** side of
planning, not the input side; the hypothesis (50–70% fewer plan tokens) is
testable but is not v1 scope to benchmark.

Discovery output is **descriptive** — observed conventions, advisory only.
Promotion to `.claude/rules/` is the explicit human gate that converts an
observation into policy. The two folders stay semantically distinct forever:
`.claude/discovered-patterns/` for raw findings; `.claude/rules/` for policy.
There is no automatic promotion.

## Scope

In scope (v1):
- New subcommand `/audit standards` (mode of the existing `/audit`, no new
  top-level command — keeps the stable 5-command surface intact).
- Multi-language structural pattern detection via `ast-grep` + `universal-ctags`.
- Tri-band confidence (≥80% strong / 60–79% weak / <60% suppressed),
  default threshold 70%, per-bucket denominator.
- `AskUserQuestion`-driven promotion into the consumer's `.claude/rules/`,
  batched up to 4 patterns per call, 3 options each (Approve / Edit /
  Reject). The Edit path returns to the agent for a follow-up Read/Write
  turn (see "Promotion loop" below).
- `--bucket <name>` flag for targeted re-scans (always a full scan of that
  bucket; no incremental machinery).

Out of scope (deferred):
- Incremental re-runs (`.last-scan`, git-SHA watermark, bucket-level
  rescan, stale-file GC). Always full scan in v1. Re-evaluate after
  measuring scan time on real consumer repos.
- Auto-injection of unpromoted discovered patterns into the planner's
  context.
- Per-plan input-side rule filtering.
- A standalone `/promote-pattern` command.
- Output-token benchmark with paired runs.
- LSP-based inferred-type extraction (heavy install, slow; reserve for v2).
- Languages beyond ast-grep's 34 built-in set.

## Architecture

### Layering (FC/IS)

All Python lives under `scripts/discover/`. There is no separate
`analyzer/` tree; that name was a drafting artifact and is dropped.

- **Boundary** (`scripts/discover/boundary.py`):
  - Parses `ast-grep --json=stream` output into typed `Match` records.
    Fail-closed on missing or unknown `language` value (validated against
    an allowlist derived from ast-grep's documented language set).
  - Parses `universal-ctags --output-format=json` JSON Lines into typed
    `Symbol` records.
  - **Normalizes ctags `kind` values to a canonical vocabulary** before
    handoff to core. ctags emits language-specific kinds (`f` vs
    `function`, `m` vs `method`, etc.); the boundary maps each known
    `(language, kind)` pair to one of: `function | method | class |
    module | variable | other`. Unknown pairs map to `other` and emit a
    warning to stderr. This map is data, not code (a YAML table inside
    the boundary module's resource directory) so adding languages does
    not require editing core logic.
  - Validates `--bucket <name>` against `^[a-z0-9_-]+$` before any
    filesystem use.
- **Core** (pure Python, `scripts/discover/core/`):
  - `bucket.py` — assigns files to buckets from path + normalized kind.
  - `features.py` — composes per-file `FeatureRecord` from `Match` +
    `Symbol` sets.
  - `cluster.py` — mode-frequency clustering over `FeatureRecord`
    vectors per bucket.
  - `confidence.py` — applies threshold bands.
  - `report.py` — renders the per-pattern markdown.
- **Shell** (`scripts/discover/`):
  - `extract.sh` — orchestrates ast-grep + ctags subprocess runs, pipes
    their output through the boundary parsers, calls core, writes
    `.claude/discovered-patterns/<id>.md` files. **All file paths are
    handled NUL-delimited** (`ast-grep --files-from <(git ls-files -z |
    tr '\0' '\n')` style; explicit `xargs -0` where appropriate; every
    expansion of a path variable quoted). The file list comes from
    `git ls-files -z` so untracked files are deliberately excluded
    (recorded as a known behavior in `SKILL.md`).
  - `promote.sh` — handles AskUserQuestion loop in the orchestrator
    agent's turn-by-turn execution. The agent is the actual driver of
    the loop; the shell only produces the input ledger.

### New files (in this plugin repo)

```
.claude/skills/audit-standards/
  SKILL.md                          # triggers on "/audit standards"
.claude/commands/audit.md           # MODIFY: add 'standards' subcommand routing
.claude/agents/discoverer.md        # NEW: drives the scan + promotion loop
scripts/discover/
  extract.sh                        # shell orchestrator (NUL-delimited paths)
  boundary.py                       # typed parsers for ast-grep + ctags JSON
  core/
    bucket.py
    features.py
    cluster.py
    confidence.py
    report.py
  rules/
    imports.yml
    export-shape.yml
    error-handling.yml
    async-marker.yml
    return-type.yml
  data/
    ctags-kind-map.yml              # (language, kind) -> canonical vocabulary
  tests/
    test_boundary.py                # contract: accept/reject ast-grep JSON;
                                    # unknown language -> reject;
                                    # ctags kind normalization correctness
    test_cluster.py                 # property: deterministic; mode-freq invariants
    test_bucketize.py               # path globs total + disjoint by precedence
  CALIBRATION.md                    # recall AND precision sample, per language
docs/templates/discovered-pattern-template.md
```

### Files in the consumer repo (created by the skill)

```
.claude/discovered-patterns/
  <pattern-id>.md                   # descriptive observation; advisory
.claude/rules/
  <name>.md                         # consumer-promoted standards
```

There is no state file in v1. Every run is a full scan.

## Behavior

### `/audit standards` (full scan)

1. Verify deps: `ast-grep --version` and `ctags --version`. Hard-fail with
   install commands (`brew install ast-grep universal-ctags`, `cargo
   install ast-grep`, `apt install universal-ctags`) if either is missing.
   No degraded mode.
2. Verify the consumer repo is a git checkout. Hard-fail otherwise.
3. Resolve file set: `git ls-files -z` (tracked files only; untracked
   excluded by design — documented in `SKILL.md`).
4. Bucketize files (path heuristics + normalized ctags kind).
5. Skip any bucket with fewer than `AIDP_DISCOVER_BUCKET_MIN` (default 5)
   members.
6. Extract features (`ast-grep --json=stream` over the 5 rule files,
   merged with ctags JSON Lines by filepath, via the boundary parser).
7. Cluster per bucket; compute confidence; apply tri-band filter.
8. **Garbage collect**: before writing new pattern files, remove every
   file in `.claude/discovered-patterns/` whose pattern id is not in the
   current run's surviving set. This is safe because v1 always full-scans
   and the file set is deterministic.
9. Write one `.claude/discovered-patterns/<id>.md` per surviving pattern
   using `docs/templates/discovered-pattern-template.md`. Each file
   records: id, bucket, confidence %, `n/N`, evidence file list, feature
   signature, and a ready-to-copy "Promote" block matching the
   `.claude/rules/` markdown shape.
10. Enter promotion loop (see below).

### `/audit standards --bucket <name>`

- Validate `<name>` against `^[a-z0-9_-]+$`. Hard-fail on mismatch.
- Run steps 1–9 but restrict bucketizing to the named bucket. Other
  pattern files are left untouched (GC limited to the named bucket).
- Same promotion loop on the bucket's surviving patterns.

### Promotion loop

Driven by the `discoverer` agent across multiple tool turns:

1. Read the surviving pattern list from `.claude/discovered-patterns/`.
2. Loop in chunks of up to 4 patterns. For each chunk, call
   `AskUserQuestion` with one question per pattern, each offering exactly
   three options: `Approve (Recommended)`, `Edit`, `Reject`.
3. For each answer in the response:
   - `Approve` → read the pattern file's `Promote` block, write it to
     `.claude/rules/<name>.md`. Append a record to the decisions log.
   - `Reject` → leave the descriptive file in `discovered-patterns/`,
     skip rules. Append a record.
   - `Edit` → enter a follow-up turn: read the pattern file, render the
     `Promote` block back to the user with an explicit prompt ("paste the
     revised content, or reply `cancel`"). On reply, write the user's
     content verbatim to `.claude/rules/<name>.md`. On `cancel`, treat as
     Reject. Append a record. **This is the only path that requires a
     separate tool turn**; document it in `SKILL.md` so the agent does
     not try to capture free text inside the same AskUserQuestion.
4. Continue until all chunks processed.

Decisions log: append one JSON record per decision to
`${RUN_DIR}/decisions.jsonl` per
`docs/templates/decisions-jsonl-schema.md`. Outside a `/ship` run
(`RUN_DIR` unset), write to `.claude/discovered-patterns/.decisions.jsonl`.

### Configuration (env vars + flags; no new config file)

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `AIDP_DISCOVER_THRESHOLD` | `70` | Lower bound of the "surface" band; `<60` always suppressed; `60–79` weak; `≥80` strong. |
| `AIDP_DISCOVER_BUCKET_MIN` | `5` | Buckets with fewer files are skipped. |
| `AIDP_DISCOVER_LANGS` | unset (all detected) | Comma-separated allow-list. |

CLI flags `--threshold`, `--min-bucket`, `--langs`, `--bucket` override
env vars per invocation.

### Bucketing heuristics (v1)

Default path → bucket map (file matching multiple globs takes the first
match in declaration order):

| Path glob | Bucket | Normalized kind filter |
|---|---|---|
| `**/test/**`, `**/tests/**`, `**/*.test.*`, `**/*_test.*`, `**/*.spec.*` | `tests` | any |
| `**/api/**`, `**/handlers/**`, `**/routes/**`, `**/controllers/**` | `http-handlers` | function, method |
| `**/jobs/**`, `**/workers/**`, `**/tasks/**` | `background-jobs` | function, method |
| `**/cli/**`, `**/cmd/**`, `**/bin/**` | `cli-entrypoints` | function, method |
| `**/db/**`, `**/models/**`, `**/repository/**` | `data-access` | class, function |
| `**/lib/**`, `**/utils/**`, `**/helpers/**` | `utilities` | function |
| everything else | `unbucketed` (skipped in v1) | n/a |

Kind filters operate on the **normalized** kind vocabulary produced by
the boundary, not raw ctags kinds.

### Calibration (one-time, v1 deliverable; manual research task)

Before publishing confidence numbers, sample 50 random files per scanned
language against this repo and **measure both**:

- **Recall** — does the extractor catch the feature when it is present?
- **Precision** — when the extractor reports a feature, is it correct?

Both numbers go into `scripts/discover/CALIBRATION.md` per language.
Acceptance bar for "production" (default-on) status: ≥80% on both. Below
that, the language is marked `experimental` in `SKILL.md` and requires
`--include-experimental` to scan. Measuring recall without precision (as
the earlier draft proposed) would not catch over-counting and would
inflate confidence numbers — both axes are required.

## Reused Code and Conventions

- `scripts/lib/project-root.sh` — for `AIDP_PROJECT_ROOT` derivation.
- `scripts/lib/style.sh` — all stdout via `style::ok` / `style::fail` /
  `style::step` / `style::header`.
- `docs/templates/decisions-jsonl-schema.md` — decisions log format.
- `.claude/rules/decision-surfacing.md` — every promotion is an explicit
  `AskUserQuestion` invocation (option #1 `Approve (Recommended)`); the
  open-decisions pairing applies.
- `.claude/rules/boundary-parse-dont-validate.md` — typed parsers for
  every subprocess JSON stream; fail-closed on unknowns.
- `.claude/rules/architecture-fcis.md` — analyzer split per the layering
  above; core stays pure.
- `.claude/rules/testing-formal-lite.md` — contract tests on boundary;
  property tests on cluster invariants.
- `.claude/agents/auditor.md` — agent contract style mirrored by
  `discoverer.md`.
- `.claude/commands/audit.md` — extended with a `standards` subcommand
  branch; existing audit default preserved.

## Critical Files To Modify

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `.claude/commands/audit.md` | Add `standards` subcommand routing; preserve existing default. |
| `.claude/skills/using-pipeline/SKILL.md` | Add intent → `/audit standards` mapping for "what are my conventions", "extract standards", "discover patterns". |
| `scripts/validate-claude-config.sh` | Warn if `.claude/discovered-patterns/` is not gitignored in the consumer repo. |
| `CLAUDE.md` (this plugin) | One sentence under "Default Command Flow" noting `/audit standards` as a documented mode of `/audit`. |

## Verification

### Unit / property / contract — TDD order

Implementer commits tests first, in this order, each as its own commit
showing a red run, then a follow-up commit showing green:

1. `test_boundary.py::test_rejects_unknown_language` — write stub
   `boundary.py` raising `NotImplementedError`; commit red. Implement the
   ast-grep JSON parser with allowlist; commit green.
2. `test_boundary.py::test_normalizes_ctags_kinds` — commit red against

# Plan: `/audit standards` — Pattern Discovery Subcommand

## Context

The ai-dev-pipeline plugin currently has two kinds of conventions in play:
**declared rules** (`.claude/rules/*.md` — FC/IS, parse-don't-validate,
security-baseline, etc., shipped with the plugin) and **the implicit
conventions a real codebase grows over time** (how this repo writes HTTP
handlers, what error-handling shape its tests use, which import style
dominates). The planner and reviewer have no way to see the second category —
they can only act on what the plugin's rules tell them. Every new plan
re-derives the consumer's own conventions from scratch, producing
inconsistent suggestions and longer plan output because the conventions are
restated rather than referenced.

This plan adds a `/audit standards` subcommand that scans the consumer repo,
detects recurring structural patterns per code role (HTTP handlers, jobs,
tests, etc.), and surfaces each high-confidence pattern through
`AskUserQuestion` so the user can promote it into the consumer's own
`.claude/rules/<name>.md`. Once promoted, the rule is `@`-imported by the
consumer's `CLAUDE.md` and becomes available to every planner invocation; the
planner can then write "follows `<name>.md`" instead of re-deriving the
convention. The expected token-saving effect lives on the **output** side of
planning, not the input side; the hypothesis (50–70% fewer plan tokens) is
testable but is not v1 scope to benchmark.

Discovery output is **descriptive** — observed conventions, advisory only.
Promotion to `.claude/rules/` is the explicit human gate that converts an
observation into policy. The two folders stay semantically distinct forever:
`.claude/discovered-patterns/` for raw findings; `.claude/rules/` for policy.
There is no automatic promotion.

## Scope

In scope (v1):
- New subcommand `/audit standards` (mode of the existing `/audit`, no new
  top-level command — keeps the stable 5-command surface intact).
- Multi-language structural pattern detection via `ast-grep` + `universal-ctags`.
- Tri-band confidence (≥80% strong / 60–79% weak / <60% suppressed),
  default threshold 70%, per-bucket denominator.
- `AskUserQuestion`-driven promotion into the consumer's `.claude/rules/`,
  batched up to 4 patterns per call, 3 options each (Approve / Edit /
  Reject). The Edit path returns to the agent for a follow-up Read/Write
  turn (see "Promotion loop" below).
- `--bucket <name>` flag for targeted re-scans (always a full scan of that
  bucket; no incremental machinery).

Out of scope (deferred):
- Incremental re-runs (`.last-scan`, git-SHA watermark, bucket-level
  rescan, stale-file GC). Always full scan in v1. Re-evaluate after
  measuring scan time on real consumer repos.
- Auto-injection of unpromoted discovered patterns into the planner's
  context.
- Per-plan input-side rule filtering.
- A standalone `/promote-pattern` command.
- Output-token benchmark with paired runs.
- LSP-based inferred-type extraction (heavy install, slow; reserve for v2).
- Languages beyond ast-grep's 34 built-in set.

## Architecture

### Layering (FC/IS)

All Python lives under `scripts/discover/`. There is no separate
`analyzer/` tree; that name was a drafting artifact and is dropped.

- **Boundary** (`scripts/discover/boundary.py`):
  - Parses `ast-grep --json=stream` output into typed `Match` records.
    Fail-closed on missing or unknown `language` value (validated against
    an allowlist derived from ast-grep's documented language set).
  - Parses `universal-ctags --output-format=json` JSON Lines into typed
    `Symbol` records.
  - **Normalizes ctags `kind` values to a canonical vocabulary** before
    handoff to core. ctags emits language-specific kinds (`f` vs
    `function`, `m` vs `method`, etc.); the boundary maps each known
    `(language, kind)` pair to one of: `function | method | class |
    module | variable | other`. Unknown pairs map to `other` and emit a
    warning to stderr. This map is data, not code (a YAML table inside
    the boundary module's resource directory) so adding languages does
    not require editing core logic.
  - Validates `--bucket <name>` against `^[a-z0-9_-]+$` before any
    filesystem use.
- **Core** (pure Python, `scripts/discover/core/`):
  - `bucket.py` — assigns files to buckets from path + normalized kind.
  - `features.py` — composes per-file `FeatureRecord` from `Match` +
    `Symbol` sets.
  - `cluster.py` — mode-frequency clustering over `FeatureRecord`
    vectors per bucket.
  - `confidence.py` — applies threshold bands.
  - `report.py` — renders the per-pattern markdown.
- **Shell** (`scripts/discover/`):
  - `extract.sh` — orchestrates ast-grep + ctags subprocess runs, pipes
    their output through the boundary parsers, calls core, writes
    `.claude/discovered-patterns/<id>.md` files. **All file paths are
    handled NUL-delimited** (`ast-grep --files-from <(git ls-files -z |
    tr '\0' '\n')` style; explicit `xargs -0` where appropriate; every
    expansion of a path variable quoted). The file list comes from
    `git ls-files -z` so untracked files are deliberately excluded
    (recorded as a known behavior in `SKILL.md`).
  - `promote.sh` — handles AskUserQuestion loop in the orchestrator
    agent's turn-by-turn execution. The agent is the actual driver of
    the loop; the shell only produces the input ledger.

### Files in the consumer repo (created by the skill)

1. Verify deps: `ast-grep --version` and `ctags --version`. Hard-fail with

2. Verify the consumer repo is a git checkout. Hard-fail otherwise.

4. Bucketize files (path heuristics + normalized ctags kind).

6. Extract features (`ast-grep --json=stream` over the 5 rule files,

7. Cluster per bucket; compute confidence; apply tri-band filter.
8. **Garbage collect**: before writing new pattern files, remove every

### Promotion loop

Driven by the `discoverer` agent across multiple tool turns:

1. Read the surviving pattern list from `.claude/discovered-patterns/`.
2. Loop in chunks of up to 4 patterns. For each chunk, call
   `AskUserQuestion` with one question per pattern, each offering exactly
   three options: `Approve (Recommended)`, `Edit`, `Reject`.
3. For each answer in the response:
   - `Approve` → read the pattern file's `Promote` block, write it to
     `.claude/rules/<name>.md`. Append a record to the decisions log.
   - `Reject` → leave the descriptive file in `discovered-patterns/`,
     skip rules. Append a record.
   - `Edit` → enter a follow-up turn: read the pattern file, render the
     `Promote` block back to the user with an explicit prompt ("paste the
     revised content, or reply `cancel`"). On reply, write the user's
     content verbatim to `.claude/rules/<name>.md`. On `cancel`, treat as
     Reject. Append a record. **This is the only path that requires a
     separate tool turn**; document it in `SKILL.md` so the agent does
     not try to capture free text inside the same AskUserQuestion.
4. Continue until all chunks processed.

Decisions log: append one JSON record per decision to

| `AIDP_DISCOVER_LANGS` | unset (all detected) | Comma-separated allow-list. |

CLI flags `--threshold`, `--min-bucket`, `--langs`, `--bucket` override

Default path → bucket map (file matching multiple globs takes the first

| `**/lib/**`, `**/utils/**`, `**/helpers/**` | `utilities` | function |
| everything else | `unbucketed` (skipped in v1) | n/a |
